title: Architecture atlas
description: A repository's walked tree and resolved import graph with its architecture manifest laid over it, as `architecture atlas` emits it. See https://dataquail.github.io/goodbones/architecture-rules/enforcement/diagram/.

path.description: The file the policy was read from — the root file, when split.

sha256.description: A hash of that file's bytes.

manifest.description: The policy this atlas was drawn against.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

fragment.description: The `defs` fragment the entry arrived through, via `use`.

allowances.description: The import allowances this node wrote itself, in manifest order. Inherited ones are on the ancestor that wrote them.

nodes.description: The manifest's tree, flattened in manifest order, each node with the pattern that selects its files and the allowances it wrote.

path.description: A walked file's path, `pkg:<name>` for a package, or `builtin:<name>` for a runtime module.

node.description: The `name` of the deepest manifest node whose selector matches the file, or null when the tree does not reach it. Always null for a package or builtin.

reach.description: Which families reach the file — `coverage`'s per-file record. A file none reaches is residue.

external.description: True for a package or builtin pseudo-file.

files.description: Every walked file and every local file some edge reaches outside the walk, sorted, then every package and builtin some edge reaches.

to.description: A walked file's path, `pkg:<name>` for a package, or `builtin:<name>` for a runtime module.

status.description: `admitted`: the importer is under an import allowlist and an allowance matched the target. `violation`: an import rule fired. `ungoverned`: no import allowlist selects the importer, so the policy has nothing to say.

node.description: The `name` of the node that wrote the allowance.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

fragment.description: The `defs` fragment the entry arrived through, via `use`.

admittedBy.description: With `admitted`: the allowance that let the edge through — the one written nearest the importer when several did.

violations.description: Fingerprints of the violations on this edge: the import rule that fired, and any exports rule about a name carried across it.

edges.description: Every resolved import, one per (importer, target) pair, with its status under the policy.

node.description: The `name` of the node the allowance is in force at.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

fragment.description: The `defs` fragment the entry arrived through, via `use`.

items.description: A walked file's path, `pkg:<name>` for a package, or `builtin:<name>` for a runtime module.

targets.description: The walked files the entry matches, from the files the node selects; `pkg:<name>` for an `external`.

used.description: Whether any observed edge passes through the allowance. False is slack: permission nothing needs, drawn as a ghost edge.

designed.description: Every allowance in force at a node with files, resolved against the walk. An allowance with no observed edge under it is slack; an observed edge with no designed edge over it is ungoverned or a violation.

fingerprint.description: kind|rule|file|subject — line-independent, so it survives edits to the file it names; the baseline's key.

ruleName.description: The manifest node path the rule was lowered from.

subject.description: The other end of the violated relationship — the resolved target, the restricted symbol, the missing sibling — or null when the file alone is the violation.

baselined.description: Carried by the baseline, so `check` does not fail on it.

route.description: For a graph `reach` violation: the files the origin reached the target through, origin first, target last.

violations.description: Every finding, baselined ones included, as the conformance snapshot lists them.

cycles.description: Every strongly connected component of more than one file, or a file importing itself, each sorted.

unresolved.description: Imports the resolver could not turn into a file, from files under an import rule. Not edges.
